message.content:
Build an honest "Trust & Security" marketing page for Nxeon at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15, Tailwind v4, TypeScript). It should build customer confidence and convert — grounded ONLY in the platform's real security posture (no fabricated certifications).

FIRST read the design-system contract: components/marketing/primitives.tsx (Section, SectionTitle, Eyebrow, PageHero), components/marketing/sections.tsx (FeatureCard, CtaBand), components/marketing/icons.tsx, app/(marketing)/vps/page.tsx and app/(marketing)/business-email/page.tsx (for structure/tone), app/globals.css.

REAL, TRUE facts to build from (do NOT invent SOC2/ISO/PCI certifications we don't have; frame honestly):
- **Isolation**: every customer runs in a full **KVM virtual machine** (hardware virtualization, not shared containers) — strong tenant isolation.
- **Network**: host firewall **drops all customer-VM → host traffic**, so a compromised VM can't reach the management plane, hypervisor, or database. Optional dedicated IPv4.
- **DDoS mitigation** at the network edge; managed firewall.
- **Backups**: automatic snapshots to a **separate ZFS backup pool**; one-click restore.
- **Encryption in transit**: HTTPS everywhere (Let's Encrypt), HSTS, secure cookies.
- **Account security**: **2FA/TOTP**, scoped API tokens, session controls, rate-limited auth.
- **Data ownership & privacy**: your server's data is yours; full root access; export and leave anytime — no lock-in. Nxeon doesn't sell data.
- **Transparent billing**: clear pricing, honest renewal prices, easy cancellation (tie-in to the honest-sales approach).
- **Infrastructure**: Singapore data center, NVMe on ZFS mirror (redundant), patched Proxmox hypervisor.

BUILD **app/(marketing)/security/page.tsx** (route /security):
- `export const metadata` (title "Trust & Security — Nxeon", strong description).
- PageHero (eyebrow "Trust & Security", a confidence-building headline) → sections built with Section (alternating base/panel tones, include ONE tone="light" band for rhythm) + SectionTitle + FeatureCard grids covering: Isolation & tenant security, Network & DDoS, Data safety & backups, Account security (2FA/API/sessions), Data ownership & privacy, Transparent billing/no lock-in. End with `<Section tone="deep" size="lg"><CtaBand /></Section>`.
- Honest tone: describe what we actually do; where something is roadmap (e.g. formal certifications), don't claim it. Use existing icons (IconShield, IconLock, IconServer, IconBackup, IconNetwork, IconCheck, IconScale, IconGauge).
- Inherits header/footer from the (marketing) group layout — do NOT add them.

Also ADD the page to navigation:
- **components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx** — add `{ label: "Security", href: "/security" }` to the "Company & legal" (or "Resources") column.
- **components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx** — add "Security" to the COMPANY dropdown array (the `COMPANY` list), e.g. after "About".

RULES: only create the security page + edit the two nav components (footer + header). Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma, app/layout.tsx, worker/*, or other pages. Do NOT run build/tsc/prisma/commit. No fabricated certifications or fake trust badges. Report the file created and the two nav edits.

This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.

- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. All done. Summary of the work:

## File created
`/opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/security/page.tsx` (route `/security`)

- `export const metadata` with title "Trust & Security — Nxeon" and a substantive, honest description.
- `PageHero` (eyebrow "Trust & Security", headline "Security you can *actually verify*") → six content sections built from `Section` + `SectionTitle` + `FeatureCard` grids, then a closing `<Section tone="deep" size="lg"><CtaBand /></Section>`.
- Section tones alternate for rhythm — base / panel / base / **light** / panel / base / deep — with exactly one `tone="light"` band (Account security), as required.
- Sections cover all six mandated topics, grounded only in the real facts given:
  1. **Isolation** — full KVM VMs, no shared containers, patched Proxmox.
  2. **Network & DDoS** — host firewall drops VM→host traffic, edge DDoS mitigation, managed firewall + optional dedicated IPv4, HTTPS/HSTS/secure cookies.
  3. **Data safety & backups** — snapshots to a separate ZFS pool, one-click restore, NVMe on ZFS mirror.
  4. **Account security** — 2FA/TOTP, scoped API tokens, session controls, rate-limited auth.
  5. **Ownership & privacy** — your data is yours, full root, export/leave with no lock-in, we don't sell data.
  6. **Transparent billing** — clear pricing, honest renewal prices, one-click cancel.
- Uses only the specified existing icons (IconShield, IconLock, IconServer, IconBackup, IconNetwork, IconCheck, IconScale, IconGauge; plus IconArrow for the "export & leave" card).
- Added an honest **"What we don't claim"** disclosure card explicitly stating Nxeon holds no SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / PCI certifications — no fabricated badges anywhere.

## Two nav edits
- `/opt/nxeon/components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx` — added `{ label: "Security", href: "/security" }` to the "Company & legal" column (after "About").
- `/opt/nxeon/components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx` — added `{ label: "Security", href: "/security" }` to the `COMPANY` dropdown array, right after "About" (also flows into the mobile drawer, which spreads `...COMPANY`).

No other files touched; no build/tsc/prisma/commit run. All icon imports are used and the `tone="light"` band inherits the design system's automatic dark-on-light foreground remapping.
